newsitem.title: CHINA: Raw cashmere price hurts China's sheep farmers.
newsitem.headline: Raw cashmere price hurts China's sheep farmers.

text.p: Sluggish prices of raw cashmere in China have hurt sheep farmers and pushed up their inventories, the China Business Times said on Tuesday.
Domestic prices have been sluggish in raw cashmere-producing provinces mainly because of declining export orders and a lack of funds among domestic purchasers, the newspaper said.

Prices of raw cashmere in the northern province of Inner Mongolia, China's largest producer of raw cashmere, fluctuated at just around 250 yuan ($30) per kg, falling sharply from 400-500 yuan per kg in the early 1995, it said.
Prices in the northwestern region of Xinjiang stood at 260 yuan per kg, while prices in Shaanxi, Ningxia and Qinghai provinces were at similar levels, the newspaper said.
Farmers were reluctant to sell their products at low prices, given expectations that cashmere prices would rebound in future, it said.

Sluggish prices have caused rising stockpiles with more than half of sheep farmers' raw cashmere output remained unsold so far, it said without elaborating. In past years, the cashmere output of sheep farmers was sold out annually.

China's top cashmere producer, Inner Mongolia Erdos Cashmere Products Co Ltd, reported good mid-term results on Monday and company officials attributed the jump in net profit mainly to a drop in the price of raw materials.

The company, favoured in Shanghai's B share trading, bucked the trend of disappointing mid-term results, with a 25 percent increase in profits over the same year-ago period to 67 million yuan despite a sharp fall in revenue.
